implementation_notes: The aggregator is replaced by a hot shared flow: MutableSharedFlow with an optional replay cache and extra buffer is the hub, publish is tryEmit/emit, and each subscriber is a coroutine collecting the read-only SharedFlow view returned by asSharedFlow() - the kotlinx.coroutines documentation uses exactly this EventBus shape as its example. Subscriptions are structured-concurrency scopes rather than registrations: collect never completes, so cancelling the collecting scope is the unsubscribe. Use StateFlow instead when subscribers only need the latest value, and a Channel when each event must be consumed exactly once by a single consumer; a Java-interop event bus or a plain callback registry is still justified when no coroutine scope exists to own the collectors.
pitfalls: tryEmit on a full buffer returns false and the event is silently dropped - publications from non-suspending code need an explicit overflow policy (BufferOverflow.DROP_OLDEST/SUSPEND) and a monitored result.
An unbuffered SharedFlow suspends emit until every subscriber has received the event, so a slow collector applies backpressure to the publisher.
The replay cache re-delivers historic events to new subscribers, which is useful for state and dangerous for commands or one-shot notifications.
A SharedFlow never completes, so collectors must run in a scope that is cancelled on teardown; there is no unregister call and leaked collectors keep receiving events.
